οἰκείων γίνεται κριτής, οὐ τῶν ἀλλοτρίων. ὁ θεὸς δὲ πάντων κριτής, ἐπεὶ πάντων
δεσπότης. 1 Kor 6,1Ἐγκαλεῖ αὐτοῖς ὅτι ὄντων ἁγίων τῶν δυναμένων δικάζειν αὐτοῖς
ὑπ' ἀπίστων ἐκρίνοντο. 1 Kor 6,2Ἄνω εἰπών· τοὺς ἔσω ὑμεῖς κρίνετε, τοὺς δὲ ἔξω ὁ
θεὸς κρινεῖ, νῦν τὸν πάντα κόσμον τῇ τῶν ἁγίων ὑποβάλλει κρίσει· ἐνταῦθα μὲν γὰρ
τὸν βίον ἀνακρίνουσι τῶν πιστῶν πρὸς ἐπανόρθωσιν αὐτῶν, ἐκεῖ δὲ τοῦ κόσμου τὴν
κρίσιν ἐμπιστεύονται, οὐ πρὸς ἐπανόρθωσιν τῶν ἡμαρτηκότων τρόπων, ἀλλὰ πρὸς
ἔλεγχον καὶ κατάκρισιν αὐτῶν. οἱ μὲν οὖν δώδεκα ἀπόστολοι τὰς δώδεκα φυλὰς
κρινοῦσιν ὡς ἐξἸουδαίωνἸουδαίους ἐξ ὧν αὐτοῖς τοῖς προφήταις ἐπίστευσαν. εἰ δὲ
ἠπίστησαν καὶ διὰ τοῦτο ἀπώσαντο τὸν Χριστόν. οἱ δὲ ἄλλοι ὅσιοι, τοῦτ' ἔστι τὰ
ἔθνη, κατακρινοῦσι τοὺς μὴ ἀποστάντας τῶν εἰδώλων καὶ πιστεύσαντας εἰς τὸν
ἀληθῆ θεόν. ὥστε οὐδεμία διαφωνία τοῦ εὐαγγελιστοῦ καὶ τοῦ 246 ἀποστόλου–ἐν
ἀμφοτέροις γὰρ ἐλάλει ὁ Χριστός–· γέγραπται γάρ· βασίλισσα νότου ἐγερθήσεται καὶ
κατακρινεῖ τὴν γενεὰν ταύτην, καὶ ἄνδρες Νινευῗται ἀναστήσονται καὶ

ἀγγέλους οὐ τοὺς κατὰ φύσιν ἀγγέλους λέγει, ἀλλὰ τοὺς ὑπηρέτας ἱερέας, τοὺς

εἴρηκεν, ἀλλὰ περὶ τῶν τάξιν ἀγγελικὴν ἐχόντων καὶ τὰ πνευματικὰ πραττόντων. εἰ

δοκεῖ τοῦτο παραλελοιπέναι ὁ ἀπόστολος, ὅπερ ἐστιν σαφές, ὅτι τὰ μείζονα τῶν
ἐγκλημάτων δεῖ τοῖς τελείοις φυλάττεσθαι. 1 Kor 6,7 Φαίνεσθε ἡττηθέντες τῷ

ἀλλήλων. 1 Kor 6,11 Μίαν τὴν ἐνέργειαν τῆς τοῦ πατρὸς καὶ τοῦ υἱοῦ καὶ τοῦ ἁγίου
πνεύματος εἶπεν ἐν τοῖς δικαίοις, τὸ ἓν τῆς οὐσίας διδάσκων. 1 Kor 6,12–13 Οὐ
προσώπου λέγει, ἀλλὰ πράγματος ἀπὸ τοῦ ὑπό τινος· περὶ τούτων γὰρ ὁ λόγος· τὰ
247 βρώματα τῇ κοιλίᾳ, καὶ ἡ κοιλία τοῖς βρώμασιν· ὁ δὲ θεὸς καὶ ταύτην καὶ ταῦτα
καταργήσει. 246,ξολ2 Οὐ περὶ προσώπου λέγει τὸ ὑπό τινος, ἀλλὰ περὶ πράγματος
ἀτόπου καὶ πάθους. περὶ δὲ 247,ξολ2 ἑαυτοῦ λέγων τοὺς ἄλλους εἰς ἐγκράτειαν
προτρέπει. εἰδὼς δὲ ὅτι τῆς πλεονεξίας αὐτῶν ἡ γαστὴρ αἰτία–οἱ γὰρ πολλοὶ πάντα
τολμῶσιν διὰ τὰς τῆς γαστρὸς ἡδονάς–διδάσκει ὡς ἀσύμφορόν ἐστι δουλεύειν τῇ
κοιλίᾳ. Οἴδαμεν ὅτι τὰ βρώματα τῇ κοιλίᾳ. ἀφώρισται καὶ αὐτὴ τούτοις, ἀλλ' ὅμως
πρόσκαιρα ταῦτα καὶ καταπαύσει αὐτὰ ὁ θεός· μετὰ γὰρ τὴν ἀνάστασιν ἀθανασίας
διδομένης περιττὴ τῶν βρωμάτων ἡ χρεία. τί οὖν περὶ τὰ πρόσκαιρα σπουδάζετε ἐξ
ὧν πορνεῖαι καὶ ἡδοναὶ ἄτοποι; 1 Kor 6,14Ὅτι τὰ βρώματα καὶ τὸ ἐσθίειν πρόσκαιρον
δῆλον. τὸ μέντοι σῶμα οὐ τῇ πορνείᾳ ἀλλὰ τῷ κυρίῳ ἀφώρισται, καὶ ὁ κύριος τῷ
σώματι· καὶ οὐκ ἂν εἴη τὸ σῶμα πρόσκαιρον, ἀλλ' ἐγερθήσεται εἰς ἀειδιότητα κατὰ
τὸν τύπον τοῦ Χριστοῦ. 1 Kor 6,15 Σῶμα καὶ μέλη λέγει Χριστοῦ, τὸ σῶμα τῶν
πιστευσάντων καὶ βαπτισθέντων. 1 Kor 6,16–19Ὅπερ ἄν τις ἁμάρτῃ πρὸς τὸ τρέφειν
ἢ ἀμφιεννύναι τὸ σῶμα, ποιεῖ καὶ κατακοσμεῖν καὶ τὴν χρείαν αὐτῷ πληροῦν καὶ
πρὸς τιμὴν τοῦ σώματος· ὁ μέντοι τῇ πόρνῃ κολλώμενος, ἓν σῶμα αὐτῇ ποιῶν τὸ
ἴδιον σῶμα, ὑβρίζει αὐτὸ καὶ ἀτιμάζει. Τὰ ἱμάτια καὶ ὁ κόσμος ἐκτὸς τοῦ σώματός
εἰσιν· διὸ καὶ ὁ ταῦτα ποιῶν ἔξω τοῦ σώματος ἁμαρτάνει, ἤτοι ὁ μὲν λοιδορῶν ἢ καὶ
ψευδόμενος ἄλλους ζημιοῖ καὶ ἁρπάζει, καὶ τὴν ἑτέρου τις γυναῖκα μοιχᾶται, ὁ δὲ
πορνεύων ἑαυτὸν ὑβρίζει οὐκ εἰς ἄλλον τινὰ διαβαινούσης τῆς ἀπὸ τοῦ πράγματος
βλάβης. πᾶν οὖν ὃ ἐὰν ἁμαρτήσῃ ἄνθρωπος, ἥμαρτεν μέν, οὐ μὴν εἰς τὸ αὐτοῦ σῶμα
οὐδὲ τὴν ἑαυτοῦ ἠτίμωσε σάρκα ὡς ὁ πορνεύσας. 248 Καὶ μὴν καὶ ἀνδροφόνος τὴν
χεῖρα μολύνων τῷ αἵματι εἰς τὸ ἴδιον σῶμα ἁμαρτάνει, καὶ ὁ λοίδορος τὴν γλώττην
ὥσπερ αἱμάττων ταῖς λοιδορίαις, ἀλλ' ὁ προνεύων, φησίν, ὅλον ἑαυτὸν βαπτίζει τῷ
pass_a_gloss: (Continuing: for of one's) own (people) one becomes judge, not of strangers. And God (is) judge of all, since master of all. [Label 1 Cor 6:1.] He accuses them that, there being saints able to judge for them, they were being judged by unbelievers. [Label 1 Cor 6:2.] Having said above 'you judge those inside, but those outside God will judge', now he subjects the whole world to the judgement of the saints: for here they examine the life of the faithful for their correction, but there they are entrusted with the judgement of the world, not for correction of the ways that have sinned, but for their exposure and condemnation. So the twelve apostles will judge the twelve tribes (Matt 19:28) as Jews (judging) Jews, from the very prophets whom they (the tribes) believed. But if they disbelieved, and because of this rejected Christ (- the conditional has no main clause). And the other holy ones, that is the nations, will condemn those who did not depart from the idols and believe in the true God. So that (there is) no disagreement of the evangelist and the [page 246] apostle - for in both Christ was speaking -; for it is written: 'the queen of the south will be raised and will condemn this generation, and men of Nineveh will rise and condemn you' (Matt 12:41-42). [Label 1 Cor 6:3.] Did he not say 'and by you the world is judged'? And now he calls angels not the angels by nature, but the serving priests, the teachers of the people, who are likely to be judged by the saints as teaching falsely about Christ; for saying 'not to speak of things of this life?' he showed that he did not speak about the angels by nature, but about those having angelic rank and doing the spiritual things. And if he called (them) angels in the proper sense, clearly he meant those who apostatized and fell from God. The priests however were called angels according to Malachi saying: 'the lips of a priest will guard knowledge, and they will seek law from his mouth, because he is an angel of the Lord of the powers' (Mal 2:7). So we judge these priests who led the people astray, likewise also those who led heresies and turned aside the teaching of Christ. [Label 1 Cor 6:4.] More choosable than the unbeliever (is) the least of the church. However the apostle seems to have left out this, which is clear, that the greater of the charges must be kept for the perfect. [Label 1 Cor 6:7.] You appear defeated by the devil not only by being judged before unbelievers, but also by the very having of lawsuits with one another. [Label 1 Cor 6:11.] He spoke of one operation of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit in the justified, teaching the oneness of the substance. [Label 1 Cor 6:12-13.] He speaks not of a person but of a thing from 'by anything': for the discourse is about these: [page 247] 'foods for the belly and the belly for foods; but God will abolish both this and these'. [Second column, pages 246-247, parallel:] He does not say 'by anything' about a person, but about an absurd thing and passion. And speaking about himself he urges the others to self-control. And knowing that the belly is the cause of their greed - for the many dare all things because of the pleasures of the belly - he teaches how unprofitable it is to be a slave to the stomach. 'We know that foods (are) for the belly.' It too has been set apart for these, but nevertheless these (are) temporary and God will make them cease; for after the resurrection, immortality being given, the need of foods (is) superfluous. Why then are you eager about the temporary things, from which (come) fornications and absurd pleasures? [Label 1 Cor 6:14.] That foods and eating (are) temporary (is) clear. The body however has been set apart not for fornication but for the Lord, and the Lord for the body; and the body would not be temporary, but will be raised to everlastingness according to the type of Christ. [Label 1 Cor 6:15.] He calls body and members of Christ the body of those who believed and were baptized. [Label 1 Cor 6:16-19.] Whatever someone sins toward feeding or clothing the body, he does both to adorn and to fill its need and toward honour of the body; but the one joining himself to the prostitute, making his own body one body with her, outrages and dishonours it. The clothes and the finery are outside the body; therefore also the one doing these sins outside the body; or: the one slandering or also lying harms and robs others, and someone commits adultery with another's wife, but the one fornicating outrages himself, the harm from the deed not passing over to anyone else. So every (sin) which a man sins, he sinned, but not against his own body, nor did he dishonour his own flesh as the one who fornicated. [page 248] And yet also a murderer, staining the hand with blood, sins against his own body, and the slanderer, as it were bloodying the tongue with the slanders; but the one fornicating, he says, dips his whole self in the (… continues in the next section).
pass_b_english: …people that a man becomes judge, not of outsiders. But God is the judge of all, since he is the Master of all.
On 1 Corinthians 6:1: He reproaches them because, though they had saints who could judge their cases, they were going to law before unbelievers.

On 1 Corinthians 6:2: Having said above, "You judge those inside, but God will judge those outside," he now puts the whole world under the judgment of the saints. Here, they examine the lives of believers in order to correct them; there, they are entrusted with judging the world, not to correct sinful ways but to expose and condemn them. The twelve apostles will judge the twelve tribes (Matthew 19:28), Jews judging Jews, on the evidence of the very prophets the tribes believed in; yet they did not believe, and that is why they rejected Christ. The other holy ones, that is, those from the nations, will condemn those who did not turn away from idols and believe in the true God. So there is no disagreement between the evangelist and the apostle, for Christ spoke in both. It is written, "The queen of the south will rise up and condemn this generation, and the men of Nineveh will rise up and condemn you" (Matthew 12:41–42).

On 1 Corinthians 6:3: Did he not say, "and the world is judged by you"? Here, by "angels" he does not mean angels by nature, but the ministering priests, the teachers of the people, who will very likely be judged by the saints for teaching falsely about Christ. By saying, "how much more the things of this life?" he showed that he was not speaking of angels by nature, but of those who hold an angel's rank and do spiritual work. If he did mean angels in the strict sense, he plainly meant those who rebelled and fell away from God. Priests were indeed called angels, as Malachi says: "The lips of a priest shall guard knowledge, and they shall seek the law from his mouth, for he is the angel of the Lord of hosts" (Malachi 2:7). So these are the priests we judge, the ones who led the people astray, and likewise those who founded heresies and twisted Christ's teaching.

On 1 Corinthians 6:4: The least member of the church is a better choice than an unbeliever. Yet the apostle seems to have left something unsaid that is plain enough: the more serious charges must be kept for the mature.
On 1 Corinthians 6:7: You show that the devil has beaten you, not only by going to law before unbelievers, but by the very fact that you have lawsuits with one another.
On 1 Corinthians 6:11: He spoke of one working of the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit in those who are justified, and so taught that their substance is one.

On 1 Corinthians 6:12–13: By "by anything" he means not a person but a thing, for this is what the passage is about: "Food is for the stomach and the stomach for food, and God will do away with both the one and the other."

The second catena form adds: He means a shameful thing and a passion. Speaking about himself, he urges the others to self-control. He knew that their greed came from the belly, for most people will dare anything for the pleasures of the belly, so he teaches that it does no good to be a slave to one's stomach.

"We know that food is for the stomach." The stomach, too, is set apart for food; yet these things are temporary, and God will bring them to an end. After the resurrection, when immortality is given, there will be no more need of food. Why then do you take such pains over temporary things, which breed fornication and shameful pleasures?

On 1 Corinthians 6:14: It is plain that food and eating are temporary. But the body is set apart not for fornication but for the Lord, and the Lord for the body. So the body cannot be temporary; it will be raised to last for ever, after the pattern of Christ.
On 1 Corinthians 6:15: By the body and members of Christ he means the body of those who have believed and been baptized.

On 1 Corinthians 6:16–19: Whatever sin a man commits to feed or clothe his body, he commits to adorn it and supply its needs, and so to honor the body. But the man who joins himself to a prostitute, making his own body one body with her, outrages and dishonors it. Clothes and finery are outside the body, so whoever sins over them sins outside the body. Or again: the slanderer, or the liar, harms and robs others, and a man commits adultery with another man's wife; but the fornicator outrages himself, and the harm of the act passes to no one else. So whatever sin a man commits, he has sinned, but not against his own body, nor has he dishonored his own flesh as the fornicator has. And yet a murderer, staining his hand with blood, also sins against his own body, and so does the slanderer, who bloodies his tongue, as it were, with his abuse.
